extracted.intended_audience: Department of the Interior staff and officials responsible for establishing or managing federal advisory committees; prospective advisory committee organizers and the public seeking FACA information
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on establishing, chartering, announcing, and administering Federal Advisory Committees under the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA) within the Department of the Interior. Covers internal DOI responsibilities, interagency implementation, and public-notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee Management Program responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of the Executive Secretariat and Regulatory Affairs develops, oversees, and coordinates the Department’s Committee Management Program, including the review and finalization of all enabling committee charters and all Secretarial appointments of actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This office supports the White House Liaison in the clearance/vetting process of Secretarial appointments. For assistance with a specific advisory committee, contact the bureaus' advisory committee coordinators (contact information provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of FACA (public knowledge and participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the FACA is to ensure that the public has knowledge of and an opportunity to participate in meetings between Federal agencies and groups that the agency either has established, or manages and controls for the purpose of obtaining group advice and recommendations regarding the agency’s operations or activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FACA exists to make advisory committee advice objective and accessible; any committee established to obtain group advice falls within this public-access purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that advisory groups be chartered
rubrics_metrics.description: The FACA requires that such groups be chartered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charters must be reviewed and finalized through the Department’s Committee Management Program as part of establishing or continuing an advisory committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance announcement and open meetings requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The FACA requires that their meetings be announced in advance and open to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide public notice of meetings and ensure public access consistent with FACA and implementing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work product public availability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The FACA requires that their work product be made available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports, recommendations, and other outputs of advisory committees should be accessible to the public (the page links to DOI's list of Federal Advisory Committees and refers to the FACA database).

rubrics_metrics.name: Government-wide implementation and GSA role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA) is a Federal law that governs the establishment and operation of advisory committees. It is implemented Government-wide by the General Services Administration (GSA), which has issued regulations and guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow GSA regulations and guidance when implementing FACA requirements; DOI administers FACA internally but GSA provides the government-wide regulatory framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOI internal administration and legal support
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the Department, the FACA is administered by the Office of the Executive Secretariat and Regulatory Affairs. Legal advice on FACA matters is provided by the Office of the Solicitor, Division of General Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact those DOI offices for policy administration and legal questions (phone numbers and email contacts provided on the page).

rubrics_metrics.name: FACA database usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The FACA database is used to manage the average 1,000 advisory committees and notify the public of their workings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the FACA database to register, manage, and publicly notify information about advisory committees; the page links to further information about the database.
